title: Cross-team engineering leadership weekly staff notes - 2026-06-22
content:
Purpose: weekly cross-team sync for engineering leadership (serving runtime, infra, SRE, platform, private deployments, product). Goal was to surface risks/blockers, coordinate rollouts, and align next-week priorities.

1) Quick wins / shoutouts
- Shipping: Canaries for model-serving v2 (smaller memory footprint + optimized KV path) reached 20% traffic without regressions; thanks to Marcus and Diego for last-minute perf tuning.
- Ops: SRE reduced noisy alerts for transient GPU driver warnings; alert noise down ~35% this week (Nina).
- Docs: Updated the Dedicated autoscaler runbook and added a troubleshooting checklist (Priya).

2) Metrics snapshot (last 7 days)
- 99th pct latency (text-generation): 220ms -> 210ms week-over-week; median stable at ~40ms.
- Token throughput per GPU increased ~8% after batching improvements merged in PR #418.
- Error budget: <1% used for the month; no SLO burn after incident mitigations.
- Cost: initial quantization experiments show ~12% lower GPU memory usage for internal benchmark workloads.

3) Major updates by area
- Serving-runtime (Marcus)
  - KV cache improvements: landed hotfix to reduce cache eviction churn for long context conversations; load tests show 6% reduced tail latency under sustained traffic.
  - Model v2 canary: rolling canary at 20% traffic; automated metrics pipeline showing no regression on output quality (we're running eval prompts as a guardrail). Next: 50% target by Thu 6/25 if no regressions.
  - Open action: finalize fallback policy mapping for v2 -> v1 for specific customer tiers (action: Marcus, due 2026-06-24).

- Infrastructure / Autoscaler (Priya)
  - Dedicated autoscaler: discovered edge case where burst_scale_down triggers incorrectly after preemption events on GCP VMs; patch proposed (SRV-1124). Patch target merge: 6/24, rollout on staging 6/25.
  - Capacity planning: added buffer for EMEA region for upcoming customer onboarding (projected +15% GPU need in July).
  - Open action: run a simulated preemption test on staging to validate fix (action: Priya + infra team, due 2026-06-26).

- Platform engineering (Liam)
  - API stability: route-based circuit breakers deployed to reduce customer-visible spikes; initial metrics show fewer 502s.
  - Console: adding per-route cost breakdown to the dashboard beta (internal) next week.
  - Open action: finalize UI copy for cost breakdown (action: Liam, due 2026-06-25).

- Private deployments (Diego)
  - Private control plane: onboarding checklist updated with new KMS/HSM validation steps after recent customer feedback.
  - On-prem package: minor installer fix for RHEL 9 path resolution (hotfix released).
  - Blocker: one pilot customer reported missing audit logs when switching retention policies; investigation in progress (action: Diego, escalate to security if not resolved by 6/24).

- SRE / Observability (Nina)
  - Incident review: follow-up from last week's transient model OOM — improved pre-warm checks added to deployment pipeline.
  - Tracing: improved end-to-end traces for multi-tenant requests; will enable sampling for alpha customers.
  - Open action: add a retrospective doc for the OOM incident and schedule review with applied-ml (action: Nina, due 2026-06-28).

- Product / Hosted API (Sofia)
  - Rollouts: internal feature flagging for structured output GA is on track; enabling to 25% traffic next week for feedback.
  - Customers: working with two customers on Dedicated migration paths; need final pricing confirmation from finance.
  - Open action: provide migration checklist to sales by 6/26 (action: Sofia).

4) Risks, blockers, and escalations
- Risk: If autoscaler preemption edge-case fix is delayed, Dedicated customers could see slower scale-up during burst events — medium priority. (Owner: Priya)
- Blocker: Private pilot missing audit logs is blocking go/no-go for a regulated customer onboarding. Consider moving them to Hosted with additional controls if not resolved by 6/24. (Owner: Diego)
- Cross-team: Need agreement on canary rollback thresholds for model v2 (quality delta, error rate, latency). Proposed thresholds shared in Confluence (confluence:SERVE-230-rolling-canary-plan). Feedback requested by 6/24.

5) Decisions
- Approve ramp plan for model v2: proceed to 50% on Thu 6/25 if no regressions in evaluation metrics and canary dashboards. (Decision: unanimous)
- Autoscaler patch: approve hotfix and staged rollout to avoid customer impact; full monitoring window required for 48 hours post-merge. (Decision: Priya + SRE)

6) Action items (summary)
- Marcus: finalize fallback policy mapping for v2 -> v1 by 2026-06-24.
- Priya + infra: merge autoscaler preemption fix and run preemption simulation by 2026-06-26.
- Liam: finalize UI copy for per-route cost breakdown by 2026-06-25.
- Diego: resolve audit log missing entries for pilot customer or escalate to security by 2026-06-24.
- Nina: publish OOM incident retrospective and schedule review by 2026-06-28.
- Sofia: deliver Dedicated migration checklist to sales by 2026-06-26.

7) Parking lot / backlog notes
- Explore more aggressive quantization profiles for medium-length contexts (applied-ml + serving-runtime). Preliminary benching shows promise but needs quality gating.
- Consider a canary health endpoint that includes model-quality signals (not just system metrics) — product + applied-ml to scope.

8) Next meeting
- Time: 2026-06-29 09:30 PT (weekly)
- Proposed agenda: canary ramp status, autoscaler rollout validation, private pilot resolution, quantization experiment proposal.

Notes prepared by: Ava Chen
Edited: 2026-06-23 (minor clarifications, added actions and dates)

Attachments: link to canary dashboard, autoscaler PR, incident retrospective draft (internal links in linked_artifacts).
